He highlighted the Supreme Court’s order directing officials to pay compensation, emphasizing accountability for administrative excesses.

item.title: Delhi Chokes: AQI crosses 400 in several areas; Smog continues to worsen | Dynamite News
item.description: Delhi’s air quality remains alarming as several areas recorded AQI levels above 400, placing them in the ‘Severe’ category. Despite a minor improvement from Friday, smog continues to blanket the city, making breathing difficult. Key locations such as Anand Vihar, Ashok Vihar, and Wazirpur reported extremely hazardous pollution levels.

item.title: Shooting in North Carolina; Four injured at Christmas event | Dynamite News
item.description: A shooting incident during Concord’s annual Christmas Tree Lighting ceremony in North Carolina left four people injured, causing panic among attendees. Videos circulating online captured the sound of gunfire and people fleeing for safety. Police immediately sealed the area and launched an investigation, though the shooter remains unidentified.

item.title: Delhi Blast: Jaish-trained doctors used household machines to make bombs | Dynamite News
item.description: New revelations have emerged in the Delhi blast case, exposing a sophisticated “white-collar terror module” linked to Pakistan-based Jaish-e-Mohammed. Investigators found that doctors associated with Al-Falah University were trained through more than 40 bomb-making videos.

item.title: Bollywood Box Office: Farhan Akhtar’s ‘120 Bahadur’ underperforms; Comedy sequel also disappoints | Dynamite News
item.description: Bollywood’s latest releases struggled at the box office on Friday. Farhan Akhtar’s ‘120 Bahadur’, based on the 1962 Rezangla battle, earned ₹2.35 crore on opening day, failing to meet expectations. Audiences gave mixed reactions, leaving producers and distributors hoping for a stronger weekend.

item.title: Delhi Crime Branch busts ISI-backed arms racket; Four held, high-tech pistols seized | Dynamite News
item.description: Delhi Crime Branch has busted a major international arms trafficking network linked to Pakistan’s ISI, arresting four accused, Ajay, Mandeep, Dalvinder, and Rohan. The gang was smuggling high-tech pistols from Turkey and China into India via drones, supplying notorious gangsters in Delhi and NCR.
